source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: WINDOW clause
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - no existing match; n1ql: namespace, '-clause' suffix per n1ql:orderby-clause convention

concepts.label: query_select (named RBAC privilege)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - distinct in shape from privilege:capella-basic-access-read/privilege:capella-advanced-access-query-read; this page cites the raw underlying server/-style RBAC privilege name directly, with no Basic/Advanced credential-type branching table. See cross_component_finding.

relations.subject: n1ql:window-clause
relations.evidence: To select data from keyspace or expression, your client must have the `query_select` privilege on that keyspace.

relations.subject: n1ql:window-clause
relations.evidence: In Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition, [aggregate functions](aggregatefun.md) can also be used as window functions when they are used with an OVER clause.

relations.subject: n1ql:window-clause
relations.evidence: In Couchbase Server 7.0 and later, window functions (and aggregate functions used as window functions) may specify their own inline window definitions, or they may refer to a named window defined by the WINDOW clause elsewhere in the query.

relations.subject: n1ql:window-clause
relations.evidence: Refer to [Aggregate Functions](aggregatefun.md) or [Window Functions](windowfun.md) for the details of window function calls.

relations.subject: n1ql:window-clause
relations.evidence: To guarantee the order of the final results, use the query [ORDER BY clause](orderby.md).

relations.subject: n1ql:window-clause
relations.evidence: the WINDOW clause must be included after the [GROUP BY](groupby.md), [LETTING](groupby.md#letting-clause), and [HAVING](groupby.md#having-clause) clauses

relations.subject: n1ql:window-clause
relations.evidence: use the appropriate [date or time function](datefun.md) to convert the date or time into milliseconds

notable_absence.finding: No management-plane capella-role gate, and critically no Basic/Advanced credential-type table either - this page's Prerequisites section names a single bare RBAC privilege ('query_select') with no credential-type branching, unlike every DDL/DCL statement page in the registry that uses the Basic->Write/Advanced->Query Index (or Query Read) pair. This is a different shape from both the management-plane gate AND the credential-type-keyed data-plane pair.

cross_component_finding: This page's Prerequisites wording ('your client must have the `query_select` privilege on that keyspace') is the raw, lowercase, underscore-separated RBAC privilege identifier also seen verbatim in server/'s and Sync Gateway's access-control docs (query_select appears in java-sdk/howtos/sdk-user-management-example.json and sync-gateway/access-control/access-control-model.json) and in this same directory's createuser.json, which observed that CREATE USER's own Purpose section describes 'the Couchbase Server Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system' rather than a distinct Capella RBAC. Taken together with that finding, this reinforces the hypothesis that the underlying privilege/role taxonomy Capella's data-plane statements check against is the same server/-derived RBAC engine, and only some statement pages have been rewritten to describe access in terms of the newer Basic/Advanced 'cluster access credential type' framing while others (like this WINDOW clause page) still describe the same underlying privilege using the older server/ RBAC vocabulary directly. This looks like inconsistent doc migration to the new framing rather than a second distinct access model.
cross_product_finding: Recurrence of the known issue in docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json: this page states 'In Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition, aggregate functions can also be used as window functions' and 'In Couchbase Server 7.0 and later, window functions ... may specify their own inline window definitions' - both an edition citation and a discrete version-number citation on a Capella page, despite Capella having neither editions nor discrete version numbers.
